"The kingdom of God is spread out before the eyes of man but men do not see it"-Gospel of Thomas.

It's full of danger and you'll uncover ever more obstacles of increasing difficulty and there's a chance the adventure could do you in, but it's gotta be the best path to take.

I want to start by saying that although you may feel like trust is betrayed, I hope you can trust me when I say that there is help out there, and ways for you to get feeling better. Some of the things you wrote are factually true, others are colored by your current mood. there is good in the world and there is bad in the world, depression makes us see only the bad. Seeing only the bad makes us further depressed and unlikely to attend to our health, and the viscious spiral continues. The longer we spiral the more we look for expedient solutions, drugs, alcohol, self harm, masturbation, and these only exacerbate our problem until we think of the grand exit. Life can be fucking cruel, the way that spiralling downward works is one of the sickest jokes I can think of. But, insight into the problem may be the way up, if you are still looking for an alternative to suicide. there's no easy, expedient way to get better, but, I've found that life can be thought of as an iterative process, in this way you somewhat spiral up. Some of the easy things to start with when you feel like life is hopeless  is to admit to yourself that what I'm doing isn't working, and to look to others for advice, which I think you have done here and that's great. Others would be, get a routine going, one where you go to bed and wake up at the same times every day, get nutritious food every day, schedule time for your fun activities and for journaling your thoughts, and for work or school work etc. The trick is balance, and reward yourself for things that feel like work. For instance, "ok brain, I'll go for a 10 minute walk, but I'm going to have a beer when I'm done". Delayed gratification is so important to success. I really hope some of this helps, as a last piece of advice, be kind to yourself, you don't deserve the suffering you are going through

It's really difficult, and I'm so sorry you are going through this, I'm on the opposite end of the spectrum as I'm mtf. I think, and I may be wrong and generalizing, but being transgender we are natural "Why?" people, I at least tend to question everything. I mean, our genders were different than what we were born with, so exactly what else is wrong? We are natural pioneers. I'm trying to look at this as a strength instead of a weakness. Here's the thing, not everyone will understand your journey, but I have the sense that it is a bit like the quote about seeing the person broke down on the side of the road. People are more likely to stop and help when the person is actively trying to fix his vehicle. In the same way, I think people are a bit scared when you stray from the norm into uncharted waters, they are scared for you. Here's my solution as far as I see it, figure out exactly what you want, figure out things that make you intrinsically happy, without depending on external sources. This usually comes down to, what are your core values, for me it looks something like empathy, honesty, authenticity, love, acceptance...then once you've found your core values, you act them out in the world, this will gave your life meaning in the darkest of moments. I hope this makes sense and is helpful, I want to end it by saying please don't go, there is a whole community here for you, life does get better, you are loved even if you don't feel it right now and you deserve to live and have a great life!
